chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Spectacular floor shows and producer Norman Thomas
summary: Clubs competed with lavish floor shows, and Norman Thomas produced the most spectacular in Chicago, at the Sunset and across the street.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you remember what the shows were like, did the do a lot of talking or --
Well the shows were, you know, they had they had what you competition shows, you know, each club tried to have the best floor show.
And they had -- they had very spectacular shows, costumes and chorus girls and dancers and singers. And there was a -- I think a fellow named Norman
Thomas, he was the best of producers of shows, night club shows, in Chicago at that time. He had the most spectacular shows of any producer in Chicago, during that time.
And where did he produce shows?

He produced shows over on the Sunset and across the street from the Sunset, I forget the name of what they call it. Club. There were two clubs, one right across the street from the other. Sunset and -- what the heck is the name of that club, where Carroll Dickerson Cal-Dixon had a band there. Forget the name of that club, I could never remember. But he was the producer of those shows in those clubs.
I think he may have done some stuff, producing at the Grand Terrace, I'm not too sure, but he was the greatest of all producers, show producers.
